author: feenberg
body:
I will go along with that reasoning, with reservations.  It doesn't seem quite right for users that want after-tax income in 2021 which is most users of Taxsim. It isn't right for users that want marginal tax rates either, since their 2021 behavior can't be affected by a  2022 change in the law.  But going along makes validation testing much easier. 

MT issued in 2023 based on 2021 income 
   https://mtrevenue.gov/taxes/montana-tax-rebates/individual-income-tax-rebate-house-bill-192/#Rebates

NM issued in 2023 based on 2021 income
   https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Rebate-deadline-address-update.pdf
  
OR apparently the rebate is a line on the form in odd years, based on the prior year income.
   https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/individuals/pages/kicker.aspx

RI I don't see a mention of this on the 2022 forms, and I can't tell when it was paid.

SC based on 2021 income but paid in 2022
   https://dor.sc.gov/rebate-2022
